user.title: Haikubox Setup
user.description: Before you start: your Haikubox must be publicly shareable. Sign in at {listen_url}, turn on the "Share your haikubox with friends" setting, and copy the serial from the public URL the site then displays.

data_description.serial: Hexadecimal code; length varies by model (e.g. 100000003d7c9f2b). Read it from your box's public URL, or its base on units that have a serial sticker.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Haikubox
reconfigure.description: Update the serial number for your Haikubox.

data_description.serial: The serial code for your Haikubox device

error.invalid_serial: No shared Haikubox found for that serial. Check that the serial is correct and that you've enabled "Share your haikubox with friends" at {listen_url}.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the Haikubox API. Check your internet connection and try again.

init.title: Haikubox options
init.description: Tune the “notable species” ranking and the unusual-visitor alert. Watched species and audio are in the sections below.

data_description.notable_rarity_weight: 100% = pure rarity; 0% = pure recency. Default 70% leans toward rarity with a small recency nudge.
data_description.absence_days: How long a known species must have gone unheard before it counts as an unusual visitor (the unusual_visitor automation trigger). Default 30 days.

watched.name: Watched Species
watched.description: Get a device trigger when specific species are heard.

data_description.watched_species: Pick from species your box has already detected. A “watched species detected” device trigger fires when one is heard.
data_description.watched_species_extra: Add species your box hasn’t recorded yet (e.g. a hoped-for visitor) — one common name per line, exactly as the Haikubox app spells it.

audio.name: Audio Options
audio.description: “Play the call” — cache and play detection recordings on the cards.

data.audio_cache_days: Extra days to cache the full feed

data_description.audio_enabled: Master switch for “play the call”. Off by default. When on, recent detection recordings are downloaded to config/www, normalized so faint calls are audible, and served locally so the cards show a play button (the source URLs expire in ~1 hour). Off means no downloads, no processing and no buttons. Needs ffmpeg (bundled with Home Assistant).
data_description.audio_cache_days: The headline detections (last + notable) are always cached for 30 days. This caches the full recent feed for this many extra days too (heavier download). 0 = headline clips only. Roughly 74 KB/clip; the cache is hard-capped regardless.
data_description.audio_norm_target: Detection clips are often very quiet, so each is volume-normalized to this peak level (dBFS) when cached. Default -3 dB. Lower it if playback is too hot for your speakers; 0 dB is loudest but leaves no headroom and can clip on some outputs (-1 to -3 is safer).

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Window lengths and poll cadence. Defaults suit most boxes — change only if you know you want to.

data_description.recent_window_hours: How far back the “Recent detections” sensor looks, and how long a species stays “recent” before it can re-fire a new/unusual/watched trigger. Default 1 hour. Longer means a fuller recent list but fewer repeat alerts.
data_description.scan_interval: How often the box is polled, in minutes (5–60, default 10). Shorter is fresher but more API load (and a faster audio/backfill cadence).
data_description.rarity_window_days: Trailing days of detection history used to rank rarity (the notable/rarest sensors and the rarity_score on events). Default 365. Shorter favors seasonal rarity; longer trends toward all-time. Rebuilt from stored daily counts on the next poll — cheap to change.
data_description.new_species_window_days: Trailing days for the “new species” momentum sensor — how many species were first heard here within this window. Default 30. Display-only; affects just that sensor.
